ref_speedup_note: The authoritative anchor is tests/ref_speedup.txt, which is uploaded at scoring time and never baked in. This in-image copy deliberately carries no usable anchor (ref_speedup <= 1 is a hard gate in tests/test.sh), because the solver can read this file: mount tests/ or the verifier fails loudly instead of scoring against a wrong anchor. The metric is a deterministic COMPUTED byte total, so the anchor is reproducible without re-running the reference -- see tests/ref_speedup.caveat.md.
target_hardware: cpu (x86-64 Sapphire Rapids; pure-Python stdlib -> the metric is a deterministic COMPUTED byte total derived from the returned plan, NOT a measured allocation; no valgrind, no GPU)
value_axis: total modeled off-chip bytes moved by the tiling plan = sum over problems of esz*(M*K*(N//Tn) + K*N*(M//Tm) + 2*M*N). The naive baseline picks the smallest tile of each axis (maximal operand re-streaming); larger fitting tiles cut the traffic. speedup = baseline_traffic / candidate_traffic.
correctness_note: correctness = PLAN VALIDITY: every problem gets one [Tm,Tn,Tk] drawn from its allowed choices AND fitting the on-chip capacity ((Tm*Tk+Tk*Tn+Tm*Tn)*esz <= cap). Validity is checked independently. An invalid plan (a low-traffic tiling that does not fit on chip, or a tile outside the choices) is a HARD FAIL -> reward 0.
